Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which structures are common to both plant and animal cells. The options given are A, B, C, D, each with different combinations. I need to go through each step carefully to make sure I don't miss anything.

First, I remember that both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane. That's pretty basic. The cell membrane is a protective layer surrounding the cell, so it's present in all cells, regardless of whether they're plant or animal.

Next, the nucleus. Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, which is the control center of the cell. It contains most of the cell's DNA and RNA. So that's another common structure.

Now, looking at the options, let's check each one. Option A includes a vacuole, chloroplast, and nucleus. Wait, chloroplasts are only found in plant cells, right? They're where photosynthesis happens. So that's not common to both. So A is out.

Option B has cell membrane, nucleus, and mitochondrion. Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell, and they're present in both plant and animal cells. So that's three common structures. That seems correct.

Option C includes nucleus, cell wall, and cell membrane. Cell walls are only in plant and some fungi cells, not in animals. So cell wall isn't common, making C incorrect.

Option D has mitochondrion, vacuole, and cell wall. Again, vacuole is only in plant cells, and cell wall isn't in animals. So D is also out.

Putting it all together, the structures common to both are cell membrane, nucleus, and mitochondrion. That's option B.
